thread:
michelle: Quick Q — Priya is moving her parental leave start up by a week. We have a ~2 week gap on the frontend roadmap. Is there an emergency childcare fund or any short-term loan program to cover hiring a contractor?

priya: Yep, unexpected early arrival. I can hand off but there’s work that needs an immediate temp. Do we have a policy for covering contractor cost or childcare emergency support? :thinking_face:

daniel: Yes — we have two separate things: a small Emergency Family Support stipend (reimbursement up to $1k/month) and a Short-Term Backfill Loan for team-critical hires (interest-free up to $5k). They’re distinct processes.

michelle: Nice — what's the simplest path for a 4-week contractor (~$4k)? Loan or stipend?

daniel: For contractor hire that large, Short-Term Backfill Loan is the path. Quick bullets: 1) Manager signoff (email to people-ops). 2) Fill the short-term loan form (link below). 3) Payroll sets up repayment via 6 monthly deductions unless you opt to repay earlier. If the cost were smaller (<= $1k) we’d do the emergency stipend reimbursement instead.

michelle: Can you drop the form link and what we need in the manager email?

daniel: Form (internal): https://redwood.internal/hr/forms/short-term-backfill-loan 
Manager email should include: employee name, coverage dates, estimated cost, justification (why must be contractor vs shifting scope), and an expected repayment plan. Example subject: "Loan request — Priya backfill 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-29"

leah: As Priya's manager I can sign. We’d prefer stipend vs loan but cost >1k so loan makes sense. Any approvals needed from finance?

daniel: People Ops approves eligibility and amount, Finance signs off if >$3k (quick review to confirm budget code and GL). For this ask (~$4k) we'll route to Finance for quick approval (usually same business day).

priya: Timing note for handoff: I can produce a 1-page runbook + prioritized tasks before leave. Will that speed approval?

michelle: Yes, send the runbook in the manager email and cc people-ops. Also include contractor rate and a 1-line on deliverables.

payroll-bot: payroll-bot: Heads up — once People Ops approves, submit the signed loan agreement to payroll@redwood.com with code `STB-LOAN` and attach a scanned ID. Payroll will configure deductions: default 6 months, pay-cycle aligned.

daniel: TL;DR action items: 1) Leah to email people-ops with manager signoff + runbook + cost. 2) People Ops will route to Finance for >$3k. 3) If approved, sign loan agreement; Payroll sets repayment. 4) If the team wants, they can split cost across two cost centers — include budget split in the email.

leah: Sending email now. Thanks — will include runbook and contractor estimate.

priya: Really appreciate the quick help, team.

michelle: One last thing — confidentiality: these supports are handled by People Ops + Payroll and kept private. If anyone asks publicly, just say "covering parental transition". :lock:

daniel: Also note eligibility: employee must be active at time of loan origination and have at least 30 days tenure. Emergency stipend rules vary for contractors vs full-time — People Ops will confirm per-case.

michelle: Great. I'll follow up once Leah's email lands and paste the approval thread here. :thumbsup:
